governingStatute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
statutorySection: Section 8 of CGST Act, 2017 read with Section 2(30) and Section 2(74)
title: Tax liability on composite and mixed supplies and classification of bundled goods and services contracts
plainTextSummary: Section 8 of the CGST Act, 2017 governs the determination of tax liability on bundled supplies comprising two or more taxable goods or services. Under Section 8(a), a 'composite supply' consisting of two or more supplies that are naturally bundled and provided in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a 'principal supply' (Section 2(30)), is treated as a supply of such principal supply and taxed entirely at the principal supply's applicable rate. Under Section 8(b), a 'mixed supply' consisting of two or more individual supplies of goods or services made in conjunction with each other for a single price, which does not constitute a composite supply (Section 2(74)), is treated as a supply of that particular supply which attracts the highest rate of tax. In corporate finance and accounts payable, bundled procurement contracts (such as hardware supply with software licensing or installation) must be tested against commercial bundling norms, single-price versus segregated billing, and ancillary versus distinct performance obligations.

keyStatutoryThresholds.compositeSupplyRule: Section 8(a): Naturally bundled supplies are taxed entirely at the GST rate of the Principal Supply
keyStatutoryThresholds.mixedSupplyRule: Section 8(b): Unbundled supplies billed for a single combined price are taxed at the Highest Rate among all components
keyStatutoryThresholds.principalSupplyDefinition: Section 2(90): The supply of goods or services which constitutes the predominant element of a composite supply and to which any other supply forming part of that composite supply is ancillary
keyStatutoryThresholds.segregatedPricingSafeHarbor: Separate, commercially independent line items with distinct itemized prices generally do not constitute a mixed supply, allowing independent statutory classification per line item
keyStatutoryThresholds.procurementRisk: Treating a mixed supply with an unsegregated lump-sum price under a lower component rate creates immediate short-payment exposure and interest liabilities under Section 50
